[Heading: Worn door balance springs]
That sounds like a mechanical issue with the door balance rather than an electrical fault. On most built-in dishwashers, including Hotpoints, metal springs or cables inside the hinge area counterbalance the weight of the door so it stays open at any angle. If those have snapped, detached, or stretched over time, the door will drop suddenly. Please switch off and unplug the appliance (or isolate it at the spur) for safety. Then open the door fully and check if you can see two springs or cables running from the hinges down into the cabinet. Are they still attached at both ends, or do any look loose or broken?
Looking under the plinth with a torch I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. The left side still seems to have some tension. I heard a twang last week when it went.

[Heading: Broken right-side door balance spring]
This is a mechanical fix. You will need to replace that specific right-side spring. Because these are often model-specific in terms of length and attachment points, I cannot give you an exact part number here. Please note your Hotpoint model number (usually on a sticker inside the door frame or on the side of the appliance) and search for 'Hotpoint dishwasher door balance spring' or contact a parts supplier with that model number to get the correct component. Once you have the new spring, ensure the appliance is isolated (unplugged or switched off at the spur). You will likely need to remove the front panel or plinth to access the hinge mechanism properly to attach the new spring. If you are not comfortable removing panels, please call an engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

The sticker's partly peeled but I can see it starts with LTF. I can't see the rest. I also can't slide the machine out, it's screwed to the worktop and the plinth is really tight. Any way to get the spring on without pulling it out?

[Heading: Broken door balance spring (right side)]
The 'twang' and visible loose spring confirm the right-side balance spring has snapped. Since the appliance is screwed down and the plinth is tight, pulling it out will likely require removing those screws and possibly detaching the plinth or worktop fixings, which is best left to an engineer if you are not comfortable with that. If you want to try a limited repair yourself without moving the machine: ensure the dishwasher is isolated (unplugged or switched off at the spur). You will need long-nose pliers. From underneath, you can often hook the new spring onto the lower hinge bracket first, then stretch it up to the upper hinge pin. This requires steady hands and good visibility through the plinth gap. If you cannot get a secure grip or feel unsure about the tension, please call an engineer to avoid damaging the hinges or injuring yourself.
